newsitem.title: PERU: Peru sees 55 pct of utility sale to individuals.
newsitem.headline: Peru sees 55 pct of utility sale to individuals.

text.p: The Peruvian government said Wednesday it expects to sell between 55 percent and 60 percent of its shares in electricity distributor Luz del Sur to Peruvian individuals in next month's planned privatization.

The government expects institutional investors at home and abroad to buy the remainder of its stake in a share placement, whose price will be set on December 10, Javier Tovar -- in charge of the sale to Peruvian nationals -- told a news conference.
The government plans to offer all of its 30 percent stake in Luz del Sur.
The sale begins November 18 with the offer of shares to Peruvian nationals under the Citizens' Participation in Privatization program, Tovar said.
The government will define the distribution of the shares it sells on December 13, he added.
"We think demand will be greater than the offer of shares and so we will again adopt a system that gives preference to small offers," Tovar said.

In July, there was so much unsatisfied local demand in the placement of state-held shares in Telefonica del Peru that the government was forced to sell a further three percent stake in the company after the original offer closed.
In the end, the Telefonica sale of a total 26.6 percent stake brought the government $1.25 billion.
The government hopes to raise $200 million in total from the privatization of its Luz del Sur shares.
Officials from investment bank CS First Boston -- chosen by the government to handle the international portion of the sale -- expect the placement abroad to raise about $100 million.
The domestic portion of the sale will be divided into two parts.
In the sale of shares to individual Peruvian nationals, Banco Continental will direct a group of local banks that includes Banco de Credito, Interbanc and Banco Wiese.

In the second part of the local sale, Spain's Banco Santander has been selected to handle the placement with local institutions. The Spanish bank's brokerage in Peru -- Santander SAB -- will direct a group of local brokerages to book-build with institutions such as local pension funds, insurance companies and banks.

In June 1994, a consortium consisting of Chile's Chilquinta International Inc and Canada's Ontario Hydro Inc bought a 60 percent stake in Luz del Sur, a former state-run electricity company, for $212.1 million.
Another 10 percent stake is owned by the company's workers.
